kurz: Hot milk with a little lemon juice curdles into flakes in seconds. Drained and pressed, it becomes a firm fresh cheese.
bild_im_kopf: Like mist gathering into drops on a cold window: at first everything is finely spread, then it clumps.
sicherheit: Boiling milk boils over easily: adults do the heating.
ergebnis: About 200 g of fresh cheese from 1 l of whole milk.
material: sieve, muslin or a clean tea towel
a plate and something heavy for pressing
verwendung: Paneer in cubes for curries: it does not melt, because it is made with acid instead of rennet.
Pressed lightly as a ricotta substitute for pasta and cakes.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Bring the milk to the boil, stirring
schluesselmomente.warum: Heat loosens the [[milch|milk]] protein (casein) so that it flocculates completely in a moment.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Heat off; stir in lemon juice a spoonful at a time
schluesselmomente.warum: The [[saeure|acid]] takes away the protein particles' charge. They stop repelling each other and clump together.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Wait until the whey is clear and greenish
schluesselmomente.warum: Then all the protein has flocculated. If it is milky, add a little more acid.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Pour into the cloth and rinse briefly with water
Wrap it up and press for 30–40 minutes
schluesselmomente.warum: Pressing squeezes out whey: pressed briefly it stays soft like ricotta; pressed long it becomes firm enough to slice.
